status: SOURCE-LED ADVERSARIAL REVIEW / EXISTING ALLEGATIONS — NOT AN ADJUDICATED CRIMINAL FINDING
scope: Concurso 36/2012 procedural classification, definitive-text control, and cumulative judge/Insolvency-Administrator conduct analysis

declared_position.es: Posición declarada de Gil Marer/Aweswell: las preocupaciones y alegaciones sobre la actuación del juez del concurso no se limitan a una resolución ni a un error aislado. Se alega un patrón acumulativo de múltiples actos y omisiones potencialmente ilícitos, falta de neutralidad, trato asimétrico, posible favorecimiento/neutralización institucional y potencial prevaricación judicial, junto con quejas y comunicaciones ya promovidas ante el CGPJ y otras vías competentes. Esta posición es una alegación formal/contextual que debe investigarse actor por actor; no es por sí misma una declaración judicial de culpabilidad.
declared_position.en: Declared Gil Marer/Aweswell position: concerns and allegations about the insolvency judge are not limited to one decision or one isolated error. A cumulative pattern of multiple potentially unlawful acts and omissions, lack of neutrality, asymmetric treatment, possible institutional shielding/neutralisation and potential judicial prevarication is alleged, alongside complaints and communications already pursued before the CGPJ and other competent routes. This is formal allegation/history requiring actor-specific investigation; it is not itself an adjudicated finding of guilt.

dry_law.es: Primero clasificar cada acto por la vía procesal histórica que realmente lo regía: incidente concursal, modificación de textos definitivos, plan/liquidación, aclaración/complemento/corrección, recurso, calificación, escrito ordinario de sección, realización/adjudicación, testimonio/firmeza o ejecución registral.
dry_law.en: First classify every act under the historical procedural route that actually governed it: insolvency incident, definitive-text modification, liquidation-plan/liquidation act, clarification/completion/correction, appeal/review, qualification proceedings, ordinary section filing, realisation/adjudication, testimony/finality or registry implementation.

adversarial_misconduct.es: Después, y de forma independiente, someter al juez y al AC a una revisión adversarial: desviación o sustitución de vía, coherencia con resoluciones propias previas, contradicción, selección de la prueba o cálculo de una parte, igualdad de armas, pérdida/reducción de contradicción o recurso, conocimiento previo, protección de la masa y terceros, beneficiario/perjudicado, repetición, causalidad, explicación jurídica alternativa y elemento subjetivo cuando se examine una hipótesis penal.
adversarial_misconduct.en: Then, independently, subject the judge and IA to adversarial review: departure from or substitution of procedural route, consistency with their own prior decisions, contradiction, selection of one party's evidence/calculation, equality of arms, loss/reduction of contradiction or review, prior knowledge, protection of the estate and third parties, beneficiary/harm, repetition, causation, alternative lawful explanation and subjective element when testing a criminal hypothesis.

no_shortcuts: Do not presume unexplained conduct benign merely because it is judicial/administrative conduct.
Do not infer criminality merely from an adverse outcome, legal error, inconsistency or benefit to another party.
Do not call an act an incidente concursal merely because it is important or contested.
Do not call a matter ignored when an adverse or partial response is located.
Preserve protective/corrective counterweights and contrary evidence in the same actor chronology.

legal_baseline.point: Incidente concursal is the channel for questions arising during the insolvency for which the Ley Concursal does not prescribe another procedure; it is not a synonym for every contested insolvency act.

legal_baseline.rule: Ley Concursal 22/2003, arts. 97, 97 bis and 97 ter
legal_baseline.point: Post-final-text changes are controlled by specific grounds/procedure. Under art. 97 bis the IA report and transfer/opposition structure matters; an adverse IA report can lead the applicant to promote an incidente concursal.

Interest on secured claims may continue to the extent covered by the respective real security. Accrual/enforceability and formal modification of the definitive creditor list are analytically distinct questions and must be reconciled rather than collapsed.

Signed judicial decisions are invariant subject to the narrow clarification, correction and completion mechanisms; clarification is not a general substitute for a different substantive procedural route.
Judicial prevarication requires an unjust decision issued knowingly ('a sabiendas'). Legal departure/injustice and knowledge are separate elements to prove; an adverse decision alone is insufficient.

procedural_taxonomy.definition: A formally opened/admitted incidental action governed by former LC arts. 192-196 or a specific LC provision routing the dispute to the incident.
procedural_taxonomy.proof_gate: Caption/docket or admitting order plus claim/parties/object and resulting incidental judgment/order.

procedural_taxonomy.definition: Specific post-definitive-text modification route under former LC arts. 97/97 bis/97 ter.
procedural_taxonomy.proof_gate: Application/ground + IA report + transfer/opposition/incident if applicable + signed modifying order + exact before/after entry + review/finality.

procedural_taxonomy.definition: Narrow correction/clarification/completion route under LEC 214-215 and LOPJ 267.
procedural_taxonomy.proof_gate: Original decision + clarification request/trigger + signed clarification/correction/completion order and its legally permitted scope.

procedural_taxonomy.definition: Plan approval, amendment/implementation and liquidation mechanics under their own insolvency route.
procedural_taxonomy.proof_gate: Plan/proposal + observations/objections + approval/implementation decision + asset/price/publicity/realisation controls.

procedural_taxonomy.definition: Reposición, apelación, queja, revisión, nulidad and related challenge routes.
procedural_taxonomy.proof_gate: Challenged act + filed remedy/receipt + opposition + decision + finality/implementation.

procedural_taxonomy.definition: The statutory qualification section/proceeding and its own pleadings, hearing, judgment and appeal route.
procedural_taxonomy.proof_gate: Section-six procedural chain; do not relabel it as an incident simply because it is adversarial.

procedural_taxonomy.definition: Ordinary party filing, IA report, DIOR/providencia or other section act that does not by itself open an incident.
procedural_taxonomy.proof_gate: Filing/receipt/treatment; promote to another class only when the court record proves the corresponding procedural route.

procedural_taxonomy.definition: Offer/improvement, adjudication, deed, set-off, possession, registry and other liquidation implementation acts.
procedural_taxonomy.proof_gate: Authority + exact assets + amount + conditions + finality + deed/registry/possession implementation.

procedural_taxonomy.definition: Court/LAJ certification and finality instruments used to evidence decisions for implementation.
procedural_taxonomy.proof_gate: Request + issued testimony/certification + challenge if any + operative use.

why_material_acts_are_not_automatically_.reason: The order expressly says it clarifies the 16 April liquidation-plan approval and invokes the non-appealability of clarification under LEC 214.4. It is not captioned or processed as an insolvency incident. Its substantive reach is precisely a legal issue to test; misclassifying it as an incident would obscure that issue.

why_material_acts_are_not_automatically_.act: Approval or clarification of the liquidation plan
why_material_acts_are_not_automatically_.reason: The Ley Concursal provided a specific liquidation-plan route; LC 192 treats the incident as the residual channel where no other procedure is prescribed.
They are review/remedy mechanisms challenging another act, not new insolvency incidents unless the statute/court actually opens a separate incident.
Qualification has its own statutory section/procedure. Adversarial character does not make it an incidente concursal.

why_material_acts_are_not_automatically_.act: Ordinary section filings and IA reports
why_material_acts_are_not_automatically_.reason: They may trigger a response, transfer or even a later incident, but are not the incident themselves.
This is liquidation/realisation implementation unless a specific dispute was separately routed into an admitted insolvency incident.
A testimony/finality instrument certifies or implements decisions; it does not itself constitute an incidental lawsuit.
They operate under LEC/LOPJ correction and completion rules, not the general incidental route.

verified_incidentes_concursales_located.caption: Pz Incidente concursal impugnación inventario/lista de acreedores (Art 96.4)
verified_incidentes_concursales_located.object: LPB sought exclusion of Garrigues' recorded ordinary and subordinated claims, alleging simulation/falsity/absence of real services.
verified_incidentes_concursales_located.result: Claim dismissed; no costs because the judgment recorded legal/factual doubts.

verified_incidentes_concursales_located.defendants: Luchy Playa Blanca, S.L. and Monterecco Sun Park, S.L.
verified_incidentes_concursales_located.caption: Pz Incidente concursal Resolución contrato por incumplimiento (Art 62 LC)
verified_incidentes_concursales_located.object: Termination for non-payment of the lease concerning specified Sun Park assets, eviction/vacating and rent claim.
verified_incidentes_concursales_located.result: Claim granted; lease terminated, vacating ordered, €2,733,923.64 plus interest/future rent and costs recorded in the judgment.

community_fees_family.status: FORMAL FINAL-TEXT MODIFICATION VERIFIED; SEPARATE INCIDENTAL CASE NOT YET VERIFIED
community_fees_family.initiating_position: LPB objected/requested correction concerning the Community creditor treatment; the IA issued a favorable report; the report was transferred and no opposition was recorded in the located order.
community_fees_family.operative_effect: The judge expressly ordered modification of the definitive texts concerning the Comunidad de Propietarios Sun Park contingent ordinary pre-insolvency community-fee credit, without a self-standing quantified amount in the located order; post-insolvency community-fee treatment was not thereby transformed into the same item.
community_fees_family.forensic_relevance: This is a procedural comparator showing that when a definitive-text entry was formally changed, the record identified the statutory modification route and the judge expressly ordered the modification. If a separate Community-fee incidente concursal exists, it must be added only when the primary incidental docket/claim/decision is bound.
criminal_led_questions: Who generated, certified and relied upon the Community fee/debt figures at each date?
Which underlying civil judgments or resolutions invalidated, limited or altered the fee basis?
What did the IA and court know about those judgments when later Community certificates were presented?
Was LPB estate treatment kept distinct from control exercised through the Community organ and from third-party title/rights?

Do later access, works, income, security or operational acts support the existing allegation that private Community/CAM actors exercised de facto or shadow control over LPB assets, and what actor-specific evidence establishes authority, knowledge, purpose and consequence?

definitive_text_change_gate.rule_es: Por Derecho no registrará que el texto definitivo fue legalmente cambiado sólo porque aparece una cifra nueva en un certificado, cálculo, Auto de plan/aclaración, informe AC, escritura, testimonio o asiento contable.
definitive_text_change_gate.rule_en: Por Derecho will not record that the definitive texts were lawfully changed merely because a new number appears in a certificate, calculation, plan/clarification order, IA report, deed, testimony or accounting entry.
required_fields: historical statutory gateway and qualifying ground
transfer/opposition and incidental route where legally required
signed judicial decision expressly ordering modification
exact before/after creditor-list or inventory entry
resulting corrected definitive list/inventory or equivalent implementation binding

8_february_2018.operative_rule: The order states that assignment changes creditor identity but not amount; amount must remain what was recorded in the definitive texts.
8_february_2018.recorded_special_privilege: €857,373.81 + €8,194,877.88 = €9,052,251.69, plus contingent enforcement costs without a self-standing amount.

4_june_2018.status: LIQUIDATION-PLAN CLARIFICATION — NOT VERIFIED AS INCIDENT OR DEFINITIVE-TEXT MODIFICATION
4_june_2018.source_mechanics: Rather than require the IA to make the prior interest calculation requested by LPB, the order relied on two CAM 17-May balance-fixing instruments and said those amounts should be followed without the prior requirement to the IA.
4_june_2018.bid_threshold: €11,887,314.33 + €1,278,518.03 = €13,165,832.36, plus continuing default interest to the extent of the respective mortgage security.
4_june_2018.remedy_feature: The dispositive portion classifies the act as clarification of the 16-April order and states no appeal under LEC 214.4.
4_june_2018.user_position: Gil Marer/Aweswell categorically disputes that this clarification was legally capable of amending the definitive texts or creating, by itself, a lawful €13m liquidation-payoff/set-off credit.

dry_law_questions: Did former LC art. 59 permit the particular ordinary/default interest used on 4 June to accrue and be exigible, item by item, within each mortgage-security ceiling?
Even if interest accrued under art. 59, was use of the resulting amount as an operative rival-bid/payoff threshold legally distinct from modification of the definitive creditor list?
Did LEC 214/LOPJ 267 permit the 4-June clarification to introduce this quantitative mechanism, or did it alter an essential term requiring another route/ordinary remedy?
Was Article 97/97 bis modification required for any change to the definitive creditor-list amount, and if so where is the order/chain?
How does the 4-June approach reconcile with the same judge's 8-February statement that assignment changes holder, not amount, and amount remains the definitive-text amount?
adversarial_prevaricacion_bias_tests: Route substitution: did clarification supply substantive relief/effect that the law required to travel through a different contradictory/remedial route?
Source asymmetry: why were CAM's own 17-May balance instruments treated as the operative amount instead of an IA reconciliation or judicially modified definitive-list entry?
Review asymmetry: did use of the clarification/non-appeal mechanism materially reduce LPB/Aweswell's ability to challenge a new operative threshold, while preserving CAM's economic position?
Prior-decision coherence: was the 4-June reasoning consciously inconsistent with the judge's own 8-February definitive-text rule, and if so was that inconsistency explained?
Knowledge: what did the judge know about the definitive-text amount, pending objections, lender-history, Community/private-control conflict and rescue routes when deciding?
Benefit/harm and causation: what concrete advantage, exclusionary threshold, loss of rescue optionality or estate effect followed from the €13.165m figure, and what intervening causes exist?
Pattern: does this act align with or cut against later adverse, protective and contradictory decisions when the full chronology is tested rather than cherry-picked?
Subjective element: what evidence, if any, supports knowledge that a resolution was unjust as required by CP 446, rather than error, disputed interpretation or another lawful explanation?
counterweights_to_preserve: Former LC art. 59 is a serious lawful counterargument for secured-interest accrual within the real-security limit and must be quantified rather than ignored.
The 26-June-2018 Auto suspended realisation of specified LPB mortgaged fincas while the appeal could affect dation conditions; this is a protective counterweight.
Other later corrective decisions, including the July-2022 deposit correction already controlled in the court-record reconstruction, must remain in the judge chronology.

cumulative_judge_ac_pattern_tests.test: Definitive amount rule versus later clarification-based €13.165m operative threshold.
Arrecife exhorto/response and actual institutional knowledge before/after the 7-June control event; identify what reached judge and AC and what protective response followed.
Alleged private control/access/locks/security/operation affecting LPB and third-party perimeter; determine authority, AC response, judicial response, estate/productive-unit effect and later use.
Court expressly recorded works/access/masa allegations and denied requested protection. Review legal basis, evidentiary treatment, alternatives and subsequent consequences; do not call it silence.

Two same-date Autos contain verified textual tension: one says auction/adjudication occurred; another says the bidding event did not take place. Test explanation, correction, defence effect and implementation.
Correction, testimonios/finality, deed and registration chain: what unresolved challenges existed and how were they treated before implementation?

complaint_context_governance.rule: CGPJ, prosecutorial and other complaint materials are maintained as an allegation-history/intelligence lane and linked to each matching judicial checkpoint. They do not prove the allegations merely because a complaint was filed.
known_context: CGPJ Diligencia Informativa 169/2026 and associated supervisory/appeal communications are present in the connected evidentiary corpus.
Separate 2026 criminal/judicial complaint material concerning alleged judicial conduct in Concurso 36/2012 is present in the connected evidentiary corpus.
Future dry-law review must ask whether each newly controlled act was already identified in, contradicts, corroborates, narrows or materially changes an existing complaint allegation.

improved_continuation_prompt: Continue the autonomous Concurso 36/2012 fact-and-truth reconstruction under this mandatory dual-lens protocol. For every material act, first classify it under the historical procedural law ('dry law': incidente concursal, definitive-text modification, liquidation-plan act, clarification/correction/completion, appeal/review, calificación, ordinary section filing/report, realisation/adjudication, testimony/finality or implementation). Then independently test the judge, Insolvency Administrator and relevant private actors against the existing cumulative multi-act allegations of non-neutrality, bias/asymmetry, institutional shielding/neutralisation, abuse/overreach of concursal powers, de facto/shadow control of LPB assets and potential judicial prevaricación — without treating an adverse outcome as a crime and without presuming unexplained official conduct benign. Preserve the Gil Marer/Aweswell position that the 4-June-2018 Auto was a liquidation-plan clarification, not an incidente concursal, and has not been shown to lawfully amend the definitive texts or convert CAM's approximately €9.052m definitive-text special-privilege amount into a lawful approximately €13.166m definitive creditor-list amount or liquidation-payoff/set-off basis. Reconcile former LC arts. 59, 97-97ter and 192-196, LEC 214-215, LOPJ 267 and CP 446 against each primary act. Require actor-specific knowledge, legal departure, procedural route, asymmetry, beneficiary/harm, causal implementation, repetition/pattern, subjective element and contrary/corrective evidence. Link CGPJ/prosecutorial complaint history as allegation context, not proof. Never call a material act an incidente concursal unless the primary docket/claim/admission or statute establishes that route. Never record a definitive-text change without the full modification gate. Close each source family end-to-end and keep the repository/site deletion-safe and publication-controlled.
